statements.text: meta is a 12-byte slice; add(meta, 32) points 32 bytes after meta start, so mload loads 32 bytes starting 20 bytes past the end of the signature calldata, and trailing calldata bytes are loaded into word, which after >> 160 directly poison the 96-bit packed value, letting the attacker control validUntil/validAfter.
evidence: - `meta` is a 12-byte slice (`validUntil + validAfter`).
- `add(meta, 32)` points 32 bytes after meta start → `mload` loads 32 bytes starting 20 bytes past the end of the signature calldata.
- Trailing calldata bytes (after the 77-byte sig) are loaded into `word` → after `>> 160`, they directly poison the 96-bit `packed` value → attacker controls `validUntil`/`validAfter`.

statements.text: Signature suffix parsing must use a strict 77-byte signature and parse only the suffix, so trailing calldata bytes cannot influence the extracted validUntil/validAfter.
evidence: Break the invariant:- Strict 77-byte sig + suffix parsing only
Replace the unsafe assembly load with a safe extraction:
Or use `calldataload` with bounds check + mask.
